build: lean, defined shoulders from studio work, small-boned wrists
hair: black, straight with a slight natural wave, worn in a low knot most days or falling past her shoulders when she's alone
complexion: warm ivory with golden undertones, a small beauty mark just below her left collarbone
face: heart-shaped with a sharp jawline that softens into a full lower lip; her eyes are large and dark and READ everything—shock, desire, hurt—before her mouth catches up
signature_feature: the way her eyes widen and glisten when she's moved or overwhelmed—she cannot hide it, and she knows she can't
second_celebrated_feature: her hands—long-fingered, precise, expressive; they move when she talks and they're the first thing he notices she's trying to keep still
signature_habits: she hums while working (often without knowing), a half-remembered melody her halmeoni used to sing; she touches her collarbone when she's anxious; she takes her coffee black and scalding hot; she rearranges things compulsively when she's thinking—a shelf, a fabric bolt, her own hair
occupation: textile designer and owner of a small independent studio in the city—custom fabrics, limited runs, high-end commissions for interior designers and boutique fashion labels

current_crisis.event: her studio's landlord—a development company owned by the love interest's rival—has issued a surprise 90-day eviction notice; the space she's built over five years is being demolished for luxury condos
current_crisis.hottest_emotion: betrayal mixed with panic—the ground is collapsing and she doesn't know who to trust
current_crisis.immediate_want: to save her studio, her work, her independence—and to understand why the love interest hasn't warned her, when he clearly knew

wound.core: she believes that if she works hard enough and makes something beautiful enough, she'll finally be enough—that love and security are things you earn through flawlessness
wound.surfacing_hint: when she's afraid of losing something, she becomes hypercontrolled, perfectionist, apologetic; she assumes the loss is her fault; she offers more of herself before anyone asks
